analysis:
Integration review of the Autopilot placements, busy reasons and transition watchdog PR. No concrete security regression is supported by the supplied evidence.

Production-code changes are narrow and fail-closed in the visible parts:
- ModelAutopilotPolicy.swift head lines 21-23 validate hold_seconds to 0...86400 and require load_model_id for a positive hold. The check sits inside the existing invalid_command guard.
- Call sites switch autopilotAllowsModel to autopilotServesModel in ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (~135, ~513), ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (~207) and ProviderLoop+Preload.swift (~30). Adoption is limited to resident, operator-selected, consented, non-retiring models with a weight hash. It ends on consent revocation, deselection, unload, self-test failure or shutdown (per the unit 8 reading of ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift).
- evictableModelSlots and idle unload now skip held slots. free_for_load_gb (ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift ~174) gives held weights no reclaim credit, which is conservative and cannot overstate capacity.
- unloadModel calls reconcileAutopilotPlacements() right after the slot is removed.
- The watchdog cancels only a stalled operation. It answers preload as failed and stops the startup preload before its next model, without clearing load or admission fences.
- The new heartbeat fields (busy reasons, adopted/held models, capabilities, transition_stalls, status detail) are consent-gated and closed-vocabulary, and carry no prompt data.
- The remaining changes are tests, docs and a wrapping resliceGateGeneration counter.
- None of this touches the encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052/T-053), key custody or SSD cache (T-041) paths.

Residual questions for later passes (the source is not in this batch, so these are unverified):
1. The exact semantics of autopilotServesModel, autopilotHoldsModel and autopilotIdleSince. They must be no looser than the replaced gates, and a hold must expire (relevant to T-029 availability and T-027 weight-hash integrity).
2. Whether holdSeconds and leaseSeconds arithmetic (Int64(seconds)*1000, Duration advance) is overflow-safe given the policy bounds.
3. The full ProviderLoop+TransitionWatchdog.swift behaviour, since only a truncated patch was seen.
4. Coordinator-side sanitization of the provider-authored `detail` text.
5. The head hunks in protocol-messages.md (~1355-1380 and 1470-1472), which were not visible.

The threat model has no Autopilot-specific entry for adoption or holds; documenting one would be reasonable follow-up but is not a regression.
